purpose: Reviewable environment contracts; statements are assumptions/models/evidence, not filesystem certification.

ENV-INPUT.statement: Filters may repeat IDs. Identity domains and sequence bounds are exploration bounds, not API quotas.

review.provided_by: API callers supply filters and identities, including duplicates.
review.implementation_obligation: Deduplicate complete scheduling keys before assigning leases; preserve the intended filter and batch semantics.
review.unproved: JSON/API decoding into verified keys and complete coordinator behavior are not proved.

ENV-RUNTIME.statement: Rust arithmetic, collections, compiler and allocator behave according to their language/library contracts. Allocation success and binary correctness are not model-checked.

review.provided_by: Rust standard library, compiler, allocator and execution platform.
review.implementation_obligation: Check arithmetic before allocation, indexing or persistent state updates; preserve failures.
review.unproved: Library specifications, compiler correctness, allocation success and compiled binary conformance are trusted.

ENV-VIS.statement: Each fresh open independently chooses missing regions. VisibleBy is an attempt number; defensive gaps can exceed documented JuiceFS behavior.

review.provided_by: Filesystem and client caches determine each fresh-open observation.
review.implementation_obligation: Actually reopen on retry and validate all requested regions within the shared retry budget.
review.unproved: Real cache behavior is not refined to the region model; no measured quantile establishes VisibleBy.

ENV-AUTH.statement: Checksums authenticate the modeled bytes without collisions; immutable references and path identities are supplied correctly.

review.provided_by: Checksum primitives and the lower-level mapping from immutable references to file bytes.
review.implementation_obligation: Authenticate the correct bytes and bind identities, lengths and offsets to the returned reference. WAL header hashes cover exactly 24 prefix bytes; frame hashes cover the full 56-byte header plus declared payload. Callers must supply those exact spans.
review.unproved: Collision freedom, cryptographic implementation and end-to-end reference/byte correspondence are not proved.

ENV-SYNC.statement: Successful file/directory sync makes preceding writes/name changes durable; errors may occur after partial effects.

review.provided_by: Filesystem, OS and storage service implement successful file and directory durability barriers.
review.implementation_obligation: Issue the right barrier after all relevant effects and propagate failures without interpreting them as rollback.
review.unproved: Actual syscall ordering, descriptor/path correspondence and service/device power-loss durability are not proved.

ENV-DELETE-FAILURE.statement: After failed deletion attempts, a retry can see current absence or a crash-restored durable name.

review.provided_by: Filesystem responses and crash recovery may preserve partial deletion effects or restore a durable name.
review.implementation_obligation: Retry deletion and required directory barriers even when a failed attempt already removed the visible name.
review.unproved: Complete crash recovery and real I/O adaptation to the modeled name states are not proved.

ENV-WAL-RECOVERY.statement: A complete uncertain frame may survive and become durable on recovery; a prior durable frame cannot disappear. Value-level model excludes byte-level framing. Storage recovery after failed catalog replay sync may lose an unconfirmed tail while the client process survives; parsed cache state is not yet confirmed durable.

review.provided_by: Storage preserves confirmed frames; an uncertain complete frame may survive, including while a client process survives.
review.implementation_obligation: Validate framing, respect the confirmed prefix, discard unconfirmed derived caches and sync recovered state before use.
review.unproved: Byte-level replay, all cache reconstruction and composition with the full queue/catalog protocol are not proved.

ENV-CATALOG-SERIAL.statement: Catalog mutation, GC scan-to-tombstone and reactivation recheck-to-owner-append serialize under a stable shared lock inode, with fresh durable state. Payload authentication may run outside the lock but cannot authorize from a stale snapshot.

review.provided_by: POSIX advisory locking, truthful device/inode metadata and a stable shared catalog inode throughout active transactions; straw must establish correctly bound critical sections and durable state.
review.implementation_obligation: Keep scan-to-mark and recheck-to-owner-append inside the correct lock after refresh. Bind every Config argument to the opened pool/run; check fresh-open device/inode against the locked log; reject uncertain cached state before all operations and successful transaction return. Physical GC may release the catalog lock only after durable permanent tombstones bind an exact plan; reacquire and refresh the same catalog before recording receipts for completed plan targets still pending, without consuming newer work.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-PEERS.statement: Other queues/readers/checkpoints obey ownership transitions; release means actual read completion, and complete transitive closures are supplied.

review.provided_by: Other queues, readers, checkpoints and their callers follow the ownership protocol.
review.implementation_obligation: Supply complete closures and retain ownership until actual reads and dependent handoffs finish.
review.unproved: Every peer implementation and application ownership lifecycle are not verified; arbitrary noncompliant writers are excluded.

ENV-CLOCK-ABSTRACT.statement: Lease expiry is a Boolean nondeterministic event; numeric clocks, drift, queueing and clock pathologies are not modeled. Externally supervised leases select executions without clock expiry; their failure detector is a caller obligation.

review.provided_by: The model supplies nondeterministic Boolean expiry; deployment clocks and lease adapters supply actual observations.
review.implementation_obligation: Check current task/attempt/epoch identity and configured expiry at the authorization point. Disable only clock expiry in supervised mode, preserve the lease mode across recovery, and require external confirmation of worker exit before retirement releases reader roots.
review.unproved: Numeric clock drift, clock jumps, delayed RPC queues and their correspondence to Boolean expiry are not modeled.

ENV-FENCING.statement: Exactly one externally fenced coordinator can mutate a queue; an exclusive_owner string is not enforcement.

review.provided_by: External coordinator ownership and fencing prevent concurrent authorized mutators.
review.implementation_obligation: Require real fencing for exclusive operation; an owner string alone cannot implement it.
review.unproved: Leader election, split-brain recovery and the external fencing mechanism are not proved.

ENV-FAIR.statement: A continuously enabled modeled action eventually runs; this is neither per-task fairness nor eventual I/O success.

review.provided_by: The modeled scheduler eventually executes each continuously enabled action required by the property.
review.implementation_obligation: Keep required work enabled and connect executable retries to the modeled actions.
review.unproved: No implementation scheduler fairness, per-task nonstarvation or elapsed-time bound follows from this premise.

ENV-STABILIZE.statement: Modeled GC/catalog I/O faults eventually stop, with no bound on preceding retries. TLA Stop stays enabled until chosen. Safety does not require stabilization.

review.provided_by: The modeled storage/failure environment eventually stops the specified crashes and I/O errors.
review.implementation_obligation: Preserve retryable state throughout the failure period and handle successful responses after recovery.
review.unproved: Deployment stabilization is not proved or bounded; this premise alone does not cause a caller to retry.

ENV-GC-IO.statement: For a permanently tombstoned pack, a successful modeled Unlink (including trustworthy NotFound) means current absence; SyncParent success persists it. Partial failure may change current/durable state. No external recreation; real stat/unlink/fsync adapter conformance is unproved.

review.provided_by: Filesystem unlink and directory sync responses for a permanently tombstoned path; peers do not recreate it.
review.implementation_obligation: Call unlink, accept only success or trustworthy unlink NotFound, and sync every affected parent before completion. Overlapping collectors must independently complete every parent barrier for their captured targets; receipt deduplication may remove only already-completed pending targets and never the permanent tombstones.
review.unproved: Trustworthiness of unlink NotFound and real syscall/controller/catalog correspondence are not proved.

ENV-GC-RETRY.statement: After a failed deletion attempt, an external caller eventually invokes GC again. This is separate from fair I/O scheduling; no built-in retry daemon or wall-clock retry bound is proved.

review.provided_by: An external caller invokes GC again after a failed attempt.
review.implementation_obligation: Keep pending deletion obligations and reset the failed controller for a subsequent invocation.
review.unproved: There is no automatic retry daemon or proof that every real caller retries.

ENV-STREAM.statement: Caller-provided payloads may return short/long traversals, empty chunks, change advertised length or ignore callback errors. Providers must terminate; arbitrary caller code is not preempted. Content equality still relies on checksums.

review.provided_by: Caller-defined providers can under/over-deliver, change advertised lengths or ignore callback errors; they must terminate.
review.implementation_obligation: Snapshot length once, check both traversals and retain callback failures even if the provider ignores them.
review.unproved: Arbitrary provider termination, trait/closure dispatch and the complete byte/hash/I/O loop are not proved.

ENV-GRAPH.statement: Reference identities denote a finite immutable graph; decoded expansion returns every record/dependency. A cached closure includes all reachable paths. Hash/JSON/I/O correspondence remains unproved; finite model also explores repeated edges and cycles.

review.provided_by: Reference decoding and the closure/cache layer provide a finite immutable graph with complete successor and cache results.
review.implementation_obligation: Enumerate every dependency, preserve identity binding and only reuse complete closures. Bind caches to pool/run/namespace and root identity. Recheck current owners and tombstones under the catalog lock after unlocked authentication. Public existing-owner reuse must cover the requested closure; reserved queue owner names bind the immutable root digest.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-READ.statement: A modeled read_exact returns all requested bytes, short EOF or an I/O error; failed attempts may have consumed a prefix but cannot authorize a root. The single-attempt scan model allows persistent corruption, assumes collision-free authentication, and does not prove real syscall termination or closure/lock conformance. A successful buffered refill can return any positive prefix bounded by capacity and snapshot remainder; read-ahead is not validation.

review.provided_by: Filesystem read responses supply full bytes, short reads or errors; a failed read may already consume a prefix.
review.implementation_obligation: Count actual bytes, reject incomplete/authentication-failed scans and never treat read-ahead as validation.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-GC-STAT.statement: Advisory stat presence may be stale in either direction. Pre-unlink stat length is diagnostic accounting, not a durability fact. Actual absence after successful unlink or trustworthy unlink NotFound is a separate ENV-GC-IO contract.

review.provided_by: Advisory filesystem metadata may report stale presence or absence.
review.implementation_obligation: Use stat only for diagnostic accounting; always issue unlink for pending paths.
review.unproved: Natural observations cannot rule out stale stat; unlink response truthfulness remains a separate assumption.

ENV-GC-DISCOVERY.statement: Managed/legacy mode is established before clients operate; hot migration is not modeled. Advisory presence stat may be stale or fail. Initial automatic discovery trusts fresh open: NotFound means no managed catalog. Later path lookups may fail or return NotFound. Real open/atomic sharing and full ownership composition remain unproved.

review.provided_by: Pool initialization fixes mode before clients operate; initial fresh open NotFound truthfully indicates no managed catalog.
review.implementation_obligation: Propagate other open errors and never downgrade a shared requirement for GC once established.
review.unproved: Initial open truthfulness, atomic sharing and live legacy-to-managed migration are not proved.

ENV-DIRECTORY.statement: Existing directory names may be nondurable after partial mkdir or failed barriers, including work by another client. mkdir failure may leave any created prefix; sync failure may leave its persistence effect. Successful directory sync persists child entries, not ancestor entries. A finite resolved parent chain reaches a stable root; directory identities, symlink aliases and mount topology are not externally changed during use. Complete create_dir_all/canonicalize/path enumeration and filesystem refinement are unproved; all resolved ancestors must be accessible for directory sync.

review.provided_by: Filesystem creation/barriers and stable accessible directory identities, aliases, mounts and root supply the resolved parent chain.
review.implementation_obligation: Account for partial creation and sync every required ancestor even if its name already exists; preserve completed earlier barriers and pending obligations after errors. A writer may cache a fully confirmed ancestor chain only after every barrier succeeds, pinning the directory inode and checking its current name; failed initialization creates no cache entry and GC parent repair remains uncached.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-PUBLICATION-RETRY.statement: A caller may retry the same in-flight publication identity with different roots and receive a conflict. A later correct retry is modeled explicitly for conditional progress. Other clients may release the original source after the durable internal hold exists; they do not directly mutate/release internal holder identities. Retry roots are complete valid immutable pack closures supplied by the lower layer; catalog changes are atomic/durable in this model.

review.provided_by: Callers may conflict and later retry correctly; peers respect internal holders and supply valid complete immutable closures.
review.implementation_obligation: Preserve old held roots while adding retry roots; release the internal hold only after a successful protected handoff.
review.unproved: Closure construction, catalog I/O and the full call-site handoff are not mechanically composed.

ENV-PUBLICATION-FINALIZE.statement: Data are already durable in a registered open file. Serialized catalog operations establish complete staging or sealing; a reported failure may leave the prior durable Boolean state or its successful effect. Caller retries after errors; eventual stable I/O and weak fairness support progress. Packed callers explicitly close before reclamation. Peers respect staging and never append to sealed paths. Byte replay, raw-reference-to-file correspondence and physical deletion are abstracted.

review.provided_by: A complete registered file is durable; serialized catalog calls can report errors after durable effects, with compliant peers.
review.implementation_obligation: Stage before sealing; acknowledge standalone publication only after both succeed and keep packed files open until explicit seal.
review.unproved: Byte replay, reference-to-file mapping, multi-file publication and physical GC are not composed in this model.

ENV-PENDING-PUBLICATION.statement: A complete file and open registration exist before a data-sync response. Sync success certifies its bytes durable; failure may have had no effect or persisted them. Peers do not replace or write these private paths. Retry authentication may encounter persistent corruption. Stable I/O, weak fairness and caller retries support eventual success or corruption rejection, not guaranteed success after data loss. Process restart, rename responses, pathname/descriptor correspondence and final ownership/GC handoff are not composed.

review.provided_by: A complete registered private file exists; successful sync certifies durability, failure may persist bytes, and peers do not replace its path.
review.implementation_obligation: Save the exact pending description before sync; fence conflicting retries, repeat unknown barriers and authenticate before returning.
review.unproved: Assignment/syscall order, descriptor binding, rename, process restart and final ownership/GC handoff are not composed.

ENV-NAMESPACE.statement: Stable in-pool symlinks may alias the same regular pack path. Resolution supplies one truthful pool-relative identity across participants and replay, including missing targets. Successful readlink returns the actual link target; InvalidInput/NotFound used for normal or missing components must not conceal a symlink. Previously absent private prefixes are created as ordinary directories/files, not replaced by aliases. Relevant namespace/alias bindings remain stable across caching and history replay. Bind-mount aliases and inode/hard-link equivalence are not unified.

review.provided_by: Filesystem path resolution and stable pool namespace, plus the lower-level straw resolver and catalog adapter.
review.implementation_obligation: Normalize pack, closure, owner, tombstone and receipt names consistently, including legacy replay; preserve canonical bindings in the cache and reject errors or escapes. Before writing path_encoding=1, normalize all owner, pack, tombstone and receipt paths. Replay may trust this marker only for compliant producers; absent markers still require namespace resolution and unknown encodings must be rejected.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-INCOMPLETE.statement: One live owning writer controls its private append path. Its saved pre-write offset identifies the entire immutable acknowledged prefix. Successful truncation preserves that prefix and sets the requested length; failed truncation may remove some/all unpublished suffix. Process restart loses this process-local cleanup descriptor.

review.provided_by: Filesystem seek/truncate/namespace responses, process identity and exclusive writer ownership; existing sync/unlink contracts provide durability and absence.
review.implementation_obligation: Capture the rollback descriptor before writing, never truncate below that saved offset, keep it across failed cleanup, sync rollback/removal before reusing the writer or sealing its unpublished final name, and reject inherited writer operations before taking their mutexes. A final name already tombstoned by GC satisfies retirement.
review.unproved: No implementation-level formal proof is retained. Actual adapter ordering, identity binding and error handling are reviewed and regression-tested; finite protocol checks do not prove arbitrary executions. See docs/DESIGN.md#review.

ENV-GC-PARENT.statement: Sealed reservations can have missing private parent prefixes after failed writer setup. Opening an existing parent may report NotFound before I/O stabilizes; this is not durable-absence evidence. mkdir creates missing unused prefixes or leaves existing directory identities/content unchanged; failed creation/barriers may already have effects. Stable names are not rebound to old directories. Deletion sync persists absence; newly created empty placeholder directories need not themselves survive for absence to remain true.

review.provided_by: Filesystem directory open/create/sync semantics, stable private namespace identities and permission to create missing prefixes; eventual I/O recovery and caller retry for progress.
review.implementation_obligation: After trusted unlink, sync an existing parent. On parent-open NotFound, recreate and sync before receipt; preserve deletion obligations through creation/sync/receipt errors. Other open errors propagate. A subsequent attempt that finds a repaired parent present still needs its deletion barrier.
review.unproved: Actual gc_io::classify, unlink and sync_parent now verify missing/error dispatch, mandatory unlink and sync/repair ordering; directory_io::sync_all verifies the actual ancestor-barrier loop. Native ErrorKind mapping, mkdir/path/ancestor enumeration, aggregate repair durability, file identity and complete GC composition remain separate boundaries. Namespace rebinding, device internals and crashed-open-writer recovery are outside this model.

ENV-WRITER-LIFETIME.layer: writer process lifecycle and GC eligibility
ENV-WRITER-LIFETIME.statement: Process execution and already-authorized storage completion are independent: kernel/server work may complete while its process is paused or after permanent process death. New process work needs a running process; timeout/suspicion or certified process death does not fence or drain in-flight work. Only the owning writer normally seals after its operation resolves. All modeled storage operations may succeed while a crashed writer leaves an open catalog reservation forever; automatic crashed-writer retirement is not implemented.

review.provided_by: OS process scheduling/death and the owning straw writer lifecycle; catalog serialization and compliant peers supply the separate ownership boundary.
review.implementation_obligation: Keep open reservations protected during in-flight operations and reject unsafe close. Writer retirement must fence all old writer operations, including work authorized before a pause, before sealing; a PID, timeout, or lock acquisition alone is not a proved fence.
review.unproved: The finite model now explicitly permits storage completion after process death, but does not refine Rust close/GC adapters, compose complete publication ownership/byte persistence, or implement durable writer fencing and drain certification. Current safety deliberately preserves open reservations after process death; failure detectors and actual stale-operation draining remain outside the implementation.

ENV-PREPARATION.statement: A new private publication name is unique and never written or rebound by peers. Catalog registration and file opening can fail after taking effect. Setup has written no payload before offset capture. A live caller retries cleanup or closes after errors; successful unlink means actual absence, and parent barriers certify durable removal, repairing missing unused parents when needed. This model does not recover a crashed writer. Dependency hold creation and release can also report failure after durable effects. A failed preparation has not exposed a complete publication, but its dependency hold remains available for retry until explicit seal/close. Multiple failed requests may coexist. A complete handoff retains responsibility for its own dependency owner.

review.provided_by: Filesystem open/unlink/directory barrier responses, unique private names, serialized catalog recovery and caller retries.
review.implementation_obligation: Save the new name before issuing registration; retain it through uncertain registration/open/cleanup errors. Retire failed new setup without deleting an existing append prefix. Capture the actual offset and preserve the same descriptor before switching to normal write rollback; resolve cleanup before reusing or sealing the writer. Track every preparation owner before its first append. Preserve failed preparations for retry, including across other requests. Explicit seal/close cleans abandoned preparation owners; retain the current cleanup identity on release errors and finish started cleanup before another request. Transfer only the completed request owner to its exact handoff; pack rotation must preserve preparation holds.
review.unproved: No implementation-level formal proof is retained. Actual adapter ordering, identity binding and error handling are reviewed and regression-tested; finite protocol checks do not prove arbitrary executions. See docs/DESIGN.md#review.

ENV-HANDOFF.layer: completed publication and caller request interleavings
ENV-HANDOFF.statement: After a failed response, callers can offer another ID, a different API with the same ID, or changed contents; they are not assumed to wait until the prior handoff completes. Successful abstract staging establishes its requested owner; failed stage/seal/consume/release may already have effects. Eventual storage stability, weak fairness and retry of the original request support conditional completion. Library return is not remote RPC acknowledgement.

review.provided_by: Caller request interleavings and catalog stage/seal/release responses; complete immutable reference closures and catalog serialization remain separate contracts.
review.implementation_obligation: Bind the complete file/cache to API and submission ID before uncertain sync; keep it active across every staging/sealing/internal hold-release step. Reject other requests before creating their holds, check pending durability before returning a cache entry, and prevent seal from discarding an unreturned description. A formerly acknowledged reference need not acquire a new unresolved guard on replay.
review.unproved: No implementation-level formal proof is retained. Actual adapter ordering, identity binding and error handling are reviewed and regression-tested; finite protocol checks do not prove arbitrary executions. See docs/DESIGN.md#review.

ENV-CONSUMPTION.layer: staging release, immutable graph recipes and post-GC retries
ENV-CONSUMPTION.statement: Reference identities name immutable direct dependency edges; successful manifest expansion returns all of them. A release response may fail after its complete catalog frame becomes durable, and peers may collect every unowned manifest before the original call retries or reopens. Other owners remain independent. Stable storage, fair scheduling and caller retry yield conditional completion only when a durable complete recipe survives.

review.provided_by: Authenticated immutable manifests, catalog locking and complete-frame replay, plus caller retries and peer ownership/GC behavior.
review.implementation_obligation: Traverse the whole requested graph, deduplicate by reference identity, validate every cached child has a definition, and persist exact direct edges in the same frame that releases staging. Restore the graph with owners on replay; discard both after an unconfirmed frame is lost. Never infer a consumed closure merely from an absent root owner.
review.unproved: No implementation-level formal proof is retained. Actual adapter ordering, identity binding and error handling are reviewed and regression-tested; finite protocol checks do not prove arbitrary executions. See docs/DESIGN.md#review.

ENV-LOCAL-ACCESS.statement: A successful local mutex attempt returns an exclusive token. try_lock returns without waiting: a held mutex reports busy; an otherwise available poisoned mutex reports poison. A synchronous fault callback may request writer access on its own thread, or wait for another caller that requests it. The outer publication retains its mutex until the callback returns.

review.provided_by: Rust standard-library mutex/token semantics, OS scheduling, and the synchronous Python callback/caller relationship.
review.implementation_obligation: Check process identity before mutex access; use a nonblocking attempt for every accessor of the NativeStore writer. Reject busy/poisoned attempts without modifying or exposing the writer; preserve the exact acquired token on success.
review.unproved: No implementation-level formal proof is retained. Actual adapter ordering, identity binding and error handling are reviewed and regression-tested; finite protocol checks do not prove arbitrary executions. See docs/DESIGN.md#review.

ENV-COMMIT-CLEANUP.layer: queue acceptance, post-commit staging cleanup and recovery
ENV-COMMIT-CLEANUP.statement: WAL acceptance can outlive an error in later staging cleanup. A serialized catalog release may be durable despite an error response; fresh replay reports durable handoff receipts truthfully. Publishers may subsequently restage the same immutable reference, and peers may collect unowned manifests. Eventual stability, fair scheduling and invocation/recovery support conditional completion.

review.provided_by: Persistent WAL/catalog prefix guarantees, fresh serialized catalog replay, truthful receipt lookup, caller retry/recovery, and independent publisher/reader interleavings.
review.implementation_obligation: Put the unique handoff identity in the accepting WAL frame. Recover pending identities before admitting newer operations or cached results. Persist the release, dependency recipes and completion receipt in one catalog frame; rebuild every receipt index if unconfirmed state is lost. Confirm the receipt before dropping pending work, and never apply an already completed handoff to later staging. Preserve protecting queue owners until cleanup completes.
review.unproved: No implementation-level formal proof is retained. Actual adapter ordering, identity binding and error handling are reviewed and regression-tested; finite protocol checks do not prove arbitrary executions. See docs/DESIGN.md#review.

ENV-TYPED-DECODE.statement: The layout matcher receives the authenticated envelope and caller descriptor fields faithfully decoded. Payload allocation may return failure; metadata allocation, process aborts and numeric memory guarantees are outside the model.

review.provided_by: straw Python/PyO3/JSON adapters and authenticated frame/index decoding provide actual and expected layouts; the runtime provides allocation outcomes.
review.implementation_obligation: Decode dimensions/length without coercion, validate local tensor shape/product, bind dtype/shape/length before payload allocation/read, and check empty typed slices too.
review.unproved: Python arithmetic, JSON/FFI correspondence, metadata allocations, placement of the matcher in the full I/O adapter and compiled code conformance are not proved.

ENV-LOOKUP.statement: After stable namespace resolution, a returning read-only open either acquires a descriptor or reports NotFound/another I/O error. NotFound does not establish permanent absence. NameBy is a conditional local lookup-attempt bound within each outer data attempt, not a measured time limit. Other errors may occur at any attempt. The descriptor binds the protected immutable reference; name resolution, blocking syscalls and returned error fidelity remain adapter assumptions.

review.provided_by: Filesystem/client read-only open responses, stable private names and caller protection of the referenced immutable publication.
review.implementation_obligation: Retry only NotFound within the independent name-lookup budget, propagate other errors, close failed data views before fresh outer retries, and authenticate data before returning success.
review.unproved: No natural name-visibility attempt bound, syscall wall-clock bound, or complete namespace/open/error/descriptor refinement has been proved. Injected errors are controlled behavior, not evidence of naturally occurring failures.

ENV-OFFLINE.statement: Offline cleanup is permitted only for a stopped single-queue namespace without catalog or queue-namespace markers. Advisory stat may be stale. A fresh read-only open returning NotFound truthfully establishes marker absence; other errors do not. Shared owners require a catalog or queues marker. Markers/owners may appear between report creation and cleanup, but all participants and namespace bindings are stable throughout the final stopped-run check and deletion. The root journal and validated immutable closure enumerate every historically accepted root pack. Failed unlink/sync may already remove unowned data.

review.provided_by: Caller-established participant quiescence, stable namespace and truthful fresh-open absence, complete root WAL and authenticated dependency traversal.
review.implementation_obligation: Fresh-open both shared-storage markers; refuse present or uncertain markers. Recheck before deletion, require stopped-run assertion and an unchanged error-free inspection, retain complete historical root closure and propagate deletion/barrier failures. Include run identity and journal files plus their resolution bindings in the retained root set; preserve full data closure with a heap frontier and validate each unique accepted root before deletion.
review.unproved: Actual quiescence/fencing, fresh-open NotFound truth, full Python/OS/JSON/graph refinement and recovery of partial offline deletion are not proved. The guard does not repair previously deleted owned files.

ENV-OFFLINE-BINDINGS.statement: A successful retained-reference trace includes every POSIX path binding used in resolution, including intermediate symbolic links and directories traversed before ..; final in-pool identity alone is insufficient. The namespace is stable against external rebinding during inspection and cleanup, but algorithm unlink actions are explicitly checked. readlink EINVAL identifies a non-symlink truthfully; other errors yield no deletion authorization. Successful cached traces are inspection-local. The required reference set includes run.json and control/journal.log, not only data manifests.

review.provided_by: Stable POSIX namespace, truthful readlink/path resolution, and the Python reference-binding traversal adapter.
review.implementation_obligation: Protect physical files and all traversed bindings for the complete accepted closure; filter sealed/pack and partial candidates alike, reject unknown identities and unlink lexical candidate names. Cache only successful resolutions/traces within one inspection.
review.unproved: Python path traversal, readlink error classification, graph expansion, report recheck and OS correspondence are not mechanically refined. The finite model supplies traces, not a full POSIX resolver. Hard-link/bind-mount equivalence and external rebinding are outside the contract; caller quiescence is not fencing.

ENV-WAL-PREFIX.statement: Serialized appends preserve every successfully synced prefix. A crash or failed call may preserve any longer prefix, including part of a frame; a failed sync may have persisted its entire effect. Three abstract units represent header, payload and trailer. Complete-frame authentication/sequence validation is truthful.

review.provided_by: Filesystem prefix persistence and serialized append ownership; authentication is supplied by the runtime decoder and hash contract.
review.implementation_obligation: Finish all frame parts before confirming, poison uncertain appends, validate and truncate only an incomplete tail, sync recovered state and seek to its exact boundary before reuse.
review.unproved: The three-unit model does not prove byte decoding, syscall/descriptor correspondence, hash correctness, real lock serialization or storage power-loss durability.

ENV-CROSS-LOG.statement: Queue and catalog have independent current and durable complete-frame prefixes. After a crash each can retain its prior durable state or its one complete uncertain frame; partial frames retain the prior logical state. Sync success is truthful; failures may already persist effects. The entry payload closure is immutable, sealed and durably staged. External reader/checkpoint/peer ownership remains active across the coordinator crash until explicitly released. Global reclamation additionally requires the application holders to finish and release; this is independent of I/O stability and scheduling. Permanent holders remain protected; per-pack progress requires permanent absence of every owner. Catalog and queue crash choices use EnvWalProjectedStates from EnvironmentWal; concrete byte-prefix behavior is separately tested.

review.provided_by: Filesystem barriers/prefix persistence and truthful framing/authentication, publication setup, serialized catalog access, and externally fenced coordinator ownership. Application completion/release is a separate progress premise, not supplied by the filesystem.
review.implementation_obligation: Make retain durable before queue acceptance; persist handoff intent/receipt, sync recovered states, retire queue references before prune, fence late retain with durable tombstones and persist deletion before receipt.
review.unproved: The projection from bytes and actual syscalls to complete catalog/queue states is not mechanically proved. The model starts after durable staged publication and omits crashed-writer recovery, arbitrary request histories, new restaging generations, JSON and real lock/fencing internals.

ENV-REPLAY-IO.statement: The replay device binds one descriptor identity throughout the attempt. Successful nonempty reads return the exact snapshot slice and advance the logical cursor; empty reads leave the cursor unchanged and may succeed past EOF; successful seek preserves the snapshot and establishes the requested cursor. Buffer discard preserves bytes/identity. Successful truncate yields the requested prefix; successful sync makes current contents durable. Failed read/seek/truncate/sync may leave arbitrary bytes/durability and an uncertain cursor, including a storage rollback; no success is inferred from Err. SHA digests bind both supplied byte spans.

review.provided_by: Filesystem byte I/O, standard buffered-reader semantics and SHA primitives; the concrete adapter must faithfully bind these operations to the borrowed descriptor.
review.implementation_obligation: Bind the opened log, snapshot, buffer and cursor to the same descriptor. Report uncertain effects faithfully and hash the exact spans. Discard buffers before mutation and preserve quarantine after failed read, truncate, sync, seek or unwind.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-REPLAY-APPLY.statement: A successful replay target application extends its abstract ordered raw-record history by exactly the supplied payload and leaves no partially applied record. Every return preserves its application context: catalog confirmation floor, run and namespace interpretation, or the queue context. Errors may leave partially changed business indexes and cannot authorize continued replay or reuse as confirmed state.

review.provided_by: straw journal/catalog decoding and business-state application. This is an implementation obligation, not an external filesystem guarantee.
review.implementation_obligation: Validate JSON and apply the decoded transaction vector in order, excluding the identity header. Rebuild all business state and derived indexes from the same synchronized prefix. Keep partial errors quarantined.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-COMMIT-APPLICATION.statement: Application callbacks can succeed, return errors, or unwind to a caller that catches the panic. An unwind bypasses Result error handling; prior durable acceptance and partial memory effects are not rolled back. A later public call may attempt collection.

review.provided_by: Rust callback/Result/unwind behavior and the caller that decides to catch a panic and make another API call.
review.implementation_obligation: Arm journal quarantine before application/callbacks, clear it only after complete success, reject further effects before cleanup/GC, and rebuild from the durable WAL before resuming. Retirement must be durable before removing its data owner.
review.unproved: The finite model uses one accepted reference and one later retirement; successful WAL, root extraction, cleanup and per-pack deletion are abstracted. Full Rust exception semantics, distributed recovery and multi-request/reader/checkpoint composition are not proved by this model. No liveness or failure-stop assumption is used.

ENV-TRAINING-CHECKPOINT.statement: The application selects a durably committed model/optimizer checkpoint and its matching consumer position. It independently retains results processed after that checkpoint, including later arrivals, until a newer matching checkpoint commits. Advancing a queue processing cursor does not commit model/optimizer state.

review.provided_by: The training application, checkpoint selection/commit logic and explicit replay data owners. straw does not choose the latest external model checkpoint or infer these dependencies from a cursor.
review.implementation_obligation: Retain any post-checkpoint replay inputs before acknowledging them as processed; persist coherent model/optimizer/RNG and consumer state; select one committed manifest; restore its matching state before resuming; release old replay owners only after replacement protection is durable.
review.unproved: The finite model uses ordered scalar positions with one input per optimizer step; it does not verify a real trainer, batching/sparse progress, numeric model updates, distributed optimizer state or external checkpoint-file publication. The integration tests exercise actual queue/store restart and GC with a mock optimizer, including explicit rejection after missing replay protection. Native API/JSON/GC refinement remains separate.

ENV-REQUEST-REPLAY.statement: Callers may retry a stable request ID/content, conflict with its content, lose a reply and reopen repeatedly. Application release and GC may remove previously accepted request data while the durable receipt remains. A replay response must not require those old files or recreate their owners. The finite RequestReplay model abstracts the lower acceptance append/sync/apply into one action; it is not a replacement for the byte WAL or cross-log environment.

review.provided_by: Caller request identities, application lifetime and storage observations; durable receipt reconstruction and early replay checks are straw obligations.
review.implementation_obligation: Rebuild request receipts from the accepted WAL, distinguish a cached null response from absence, reject conflicting content and resolve a recorded request before dereferencing its retired data. Check consumer authorization independently.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-CROSS-COMPOSITION.statement: Composition transitions expose independent durable queue/catalog effects, including acceptance with lost apply/reply and arbitrary repeated recovery. Immutable complete publication recipes and initially durable payloads/names are inputs. Crashes may restore unsynced deletions but cannot erase protected durable names. Queue namespaces and single-owner fencing are supplied separately; no atomic transaction spanning logs is assumed.

review.provided_by: Filesystem persistence supplies deletion restoration/sync semantics. straw supplies durable lower-effect linearization, complete immutable closure recipes, queue/holder/staging namespace separation and truthful recovered receipts; deployment supplies coordinator fencing.
review.implementation_obligation: Bind publication/retain to complete closures; make acceptance and retirement durable before cleanup/prune. Reconstruct exact receipts and caches after recovery. Check current attempt/epoch for new admissions; replay matching accepted receipts before validating retired payloads.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-WRITER-RETIREMENT.layer: writer retirement and durable operation recovery
ENV-WRITER-RETIREMENT.statement: A writer incarnation uses one permanent gate inode and never removes its fence or retirement markers. A paused writer cannot pass its held gate to a retiree; after process death, previously submitted I/O must finish or be cancelled before gate handoff (EnvGateMayPass). Advisory-lock acquisition alone does not establish this property. Successful file and directory synchronization faithfully persist their effects; errors may follow effects. Operation evidence is durable before preparation ownership, every recoverable result is staged before any registered preparation owner is released, and a retirement receipt follows fencing, draining, reconciliation and sealing. Fairness and eventual writer exit/effect availability are required only for conditional progress. After lock handoff, the fence observation must be fresh/coherent with the prior durable fence; a stale negative directory-entry cache cannot authorize the retired writer.

review.provided_by: OS/filesystem gate exclusion, process-exit descriptor handling, completion/cancellation of submitted I/O, immutable namespace identities and synchronization semantics; application scheduling and repeated retirement calls supply progress.
review.implementation_obligation: Bind every Store mutation to its exact incarnation gate, check the durable fence while holding it, register exact operation/owner/dependency evidence before holds, replay uncertain registry outcomes, stage all recovered results before releasing exact preparation owners, preserve unrelated owners, drain physical files, seal reservations and persist the receipt last. Parse and validate the registry without accepting invented completion evidence. The checked writer_ownership loops must validate every selected owner against registry evidence, cover each held path using dependencies registered for that same owner, and select precisely the unsealed packs whose canonical parent matches the writer directory. Native catalog snapshots, dependency-closure certification and canonical-parent comparison remain separate leaf correspondences. Recovery authenticates complete registered results before staging; permanently corrupt results reject recover, while abandon makes no readable-result claim. Reuse registry state only after reacquiring and checking the exact gate/fence and fresh log identity/length, with an entirely confirmed and applied prefix. Mark the registry cache uncertain before append/application, including caught unwind, and rebuild it after any uncertain outcome.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.

ENV-CATALOG-HISTORY.statement: Catalog model steps represent independently durable transactions. Mapping actual locked refresh, append, replay and failures to these steps is a straw obligation, not a filesystem guarantee.

review.provided_by: The real catalog adapter must supply a history corresponding to serialized durable model transitions.
review.implementation_obligation: Map lock, refresh, validation, append, sync, replay and partial failures to permitted model steps. Reject malformed/non-applicable events before WAL effects and apply the admitted operation sequence after synchronization.
review.unproved: TLC checks finite protocol instances; native API regressions and call-chain review check concrete implementations. There is no implementation-level or unbounded refinement proof. See docs/DESIGN.md#review for actual entry points, failure windows and external premises.
